🛡️ **F-SRV-1 (attended 2026-10-22; the owner: "I think there were some exploits recently - can you check on updating our server?") — THE DROPLET'S PACKAGES ARE CURRENT BUT THE MACHINE HAS NOT REBOOTED SINCE 2026-02-02, SO TWENTY KERNEL UPDATES AND THE LIBC UPDATES ARE INSTALLED AND INERT; NODE 26.4.0 IS TWO SECURITY RELEASES BEHIND.** Measured read-only: Ubuntu 24.04.3, kernel RUNNING 6.8.0-71 while 6.8.0-147 is installed (`/var/run/reboot-required` lists every kernel and libc6 update since February; `needrestart`: 4 services on old libraries, kernel verdict "reboot"); nginx 1.24.0-2ubuntu7.18 is Ubuntu's current build and its changelog names 20 CVEs of 2025 to 2026 as fixed (incl. CVE-2026-42533 "DoS and possible code execution via map directive", CVE-2026-60005), while three medium 2026 CVEs whose upstream ranges include 1.24.0 (CVE-2026-15176, CVE-2026-97629, CVE-2026-97205; fixed upstream in 1.30.6/1.31.7) are "needs-triage" at Ubuntu, i.e. not yet backported; unattended-upgrades runs daily and applied ca-certificates, xz-utils, liblzma5 this morning; 74 non-security updates pending; OpenSSL 3.0.13 (Ubuntu-patched); the ledger listens on loopback only; exposed ports 22 (keys only), 80, 443; ufw inactive; the HTTPS server block is TLSv1.2/1.3 (certbot) while the global nginx.conf default line still lists TLSv1/1.1 (untidy, not effective). Node: the ledger, the assay worker and the ledger backup run nvm 26.4.0 (2026-06-24); nodejs.org shipped July 2026 (fixed 26.5.1) and October 2026 (fixed 26.12.1, 2026-10-21) security releases with high-severity items, and the ledger parses HTTP nginx forwards from the public. The pin "26.4.0 exactly" is the replay-determinism law, so the move is a measured task: `assay-node-26-12-1` (lane-d). Tooling: `scripts/attended/droplet-maintenance.sh` (status / upgrade / tls-tidy / reboot / node; every write gated on the owner's word). OWNER DECISIONS: (1) a maintenance window now (apt upgrade, the TLS tidy, a reboot of about two minutes; nginx, the ledger and the assay worker return by systemd); (2) the Node switch on the droplet once the task's proof lands. Nginx itself: nothing to do today; Ubuntu's backport of the three medium CVEs arrives through unattended-upgrades. ✅ **MAINTENANCE WINDOW DONE 2026-10-22T10:07Z (owner: "maintenance go"):** `droplet-maintenance.sh upgrade` applied the pending updates (6 phased non-security packages remain: fwupd, glib, tmux; unattended-upgrades keeps them), `tls-tidy` set the global `ssl_protocols` to TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3 (backup `/etc/nginx/nginx.conf.before-tls-20261022T100518Z`, `nginx -t` ok, reload; TLS 1.0 now refused at the edge), `reboot` at 10:05:36Z: back on kernel 6.8.0-147 with nginx, the ledger and the assay worker active and public health `landing=200 game=200 api=200` by 10:06:31Z (under a minute dark), `reboot-required` cleared, 0 services on old libraries. Remaining for the owner: **node go** (the droplet's 26.4.0 → 26.12.1 switch; the repo's pin #76 is ahead of the box). ✅ **NODE SWITCH DONE 2026-10-23T01:56Z (owner: "node go"):** the droplet's ledger, assay worker and ledger backup run Node 26.12.1; the worker's engine copy synced first by the deploy script's own mirror allowlist (10 files, 0 deletions, rollback dir `/opt/goldrush-prev-<stamp>`; it was one deploy behind because the asn1 deploy's sync had failed, F-SRV-3), `ASSAY_BUILD_ID` aligned to the deployed build `299b1db5`, units backed up and repointed, ledger restarted and answering before the worker restarted. Verified: both active on v26.12.1 with 0 restarts, 0 version refusals, 0 backoffs, ledger 200 JSON locally and publicly, the box's engine hash `aa1435e2…` identical to main's and registered, health 200/200/200. A first attempt at 01:52Z rolled itself back on a false positive of the attended gate (it read the worker's harmless first-second "fetch failed" backoff, caused by restarting the ledger in the same command, as a refusal); the rollback worked and the corrected sequence is now `scripts/attended/droplet-maintenance.sh node <ver>`. The mirror also refreshed the droplet's `ops/droplet/edge-watch.sh` (argv[]=/usr/bin/bash /opt/goldrush/ops/droplet/edge-watch.sh ), so the JSON-aware API probe from `api-probe-json-1` is live there too.

🔕 **F-SRV-3 (attended 2026-10-23) — A FAILED DROPLET SYNC DURING A DEPLOY IS SILENT AND UNDIAGNOSABLE.** The asn1 deploy (build `299b1db5`, 2026-10-22T09:28Z) printed "ASSAYER SYNC FAILED mid-step" into a deploy log nobody read; the droplet's assay worker kept the previous engine copy for about sixteen hours, until the owner's Node switch; the cause is unknowable because `scripts/deploy.sh` sends the rsync and ssh stderr to /dev/null (the same mirror ran by hand with rc 0). Corrective `assayer-sync-visibility-1` authored and queued (lane-a): keep and print the scrubbed stderr, a drift marker, an hourly health alert while the box is behind, a rostered guard.

🔔 **ASSAYER SYNC VISIBILITY 1 — `assayer-sync-visibility-1` AUTHORED AND QUEUED 2026-10-23 on lane-a (Astra); F-SRV-3.** GATE: the fixture's FAILED output shows the cause with no IP; the marker appears on failure and clears on success; the health alert fires only with the marker; guard rostered.
